topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She watches the web glisten like glass,
how morning rewrites what the night could not pass.
The world holds its breath in a quiet, still,
and she thinks of you far on some distant hill.
I tucked your old batteries far away,
they're ghosts from a time we used to play.
I hold them now in my careful hands,
while your new ones hum inside their stands.
He hums an old radio hit out of tune,
with eyes on the clouds and the waning moon.
A weathered hand holds his chipped tin cup,
he grins and gives thanks, tipping his cap up.
You left the window wide open your own way,
letting every storm echo into the day.
Now the sky's a pale gray, not even blue,
but I still hear your voice, drifting through.
You spot a puddle and you laugh and you go,
your mom says "wait," but you just don't know.
Mud splashes your socks, your shoes are a mess,
your jeans are soaked now, your look's a disaster dress.
You dig your hoard in the same old ground,
where roots and stones keep rewriting what you found.
You think you know the way through winter's gray,
but time and frost steal your secret away.
I lift my toast to admire how it turns gold,
a little melted, but still looks bold.
The butter was solid, now it's starting to run—
maybe it got too close to the kitchen sun.
At noon it beeps like it's playing some weird noon,
a broken robot trying out new tune.
It spits out foam with an angry steam,
while the boss pretends she's not about to scream.
I sit on the bench in the late afternoon park,
their laughter takes flight from some secret spark.
I watch as they climb up the rusted old swing,
and whisper a wish—this is life's only good thing.
She sets her burger down on the greasy plate,
and scoots your fries toward her in a debate.
You pause mid-chew, eyes locked on her nap,
aware it's already too late, right or trap.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You found a small note with no name or clue,
but it said "Think happy thoughts" in bold, blue.
You flipped the card over, no more to flip,
just a quiet smile and a warm little slip.
Her rental van is packed and her patience is van,
She swears she's never been this hot since the last fan.
We inch past trucks with a little too much gas,
while she counts exits, trying not to crash or pass.
The can let out a final, messy pop,
and dribbled down where the wires used to crop.
Now every sound it makes is scratchy or blast,
like their music died the moment it passed.
The raindrops fall with a soft, familiar sound,
They drum the roof like she once did on the ground.
I picture her smile behind my closed eyes, her face,
And wish I were back where we used to embrace.
She leaves her phone on vibrate near the call,
waiting for a text to climb every wall.
Her ringtone blares loud but never plays the song,
just echoes her hope through the silence so long.
You can't look away from that late-night glow,
your brain says sleep but your thumbs still know.
The phone buzzes soft like a plugged-in wire,
but you're not a teen—you're just lighting a fire.
A dog's loud voice breaks the bus's hush,
I smile through the noise—there's nowhere else to rush.
Its wagging tail tells a story with flair,
I follow its joy through the strangers' stare.
Ten minutes is all you can spare for this time,
you skip ahead so the plot feels like a crime.
But you wish you could spend more and not miss
the joy of the story, brief as it is bliss.
I showed up ten minutes fashionably late,
we ordered food but forgot to share our plate.
I tried to read the vibe but missed the sign,
you said "my treat" and left my latte mine.
She taps the desk and calls the whole class,
her voice cutting through the quiet like glass.
With a ruler in her grip, she makes it stand,
and leads the room from her steady hand.
My toast got stuck in the middle, no pop,
it hummed like it had one more job to stop.
I gave it a nudge with my spoon and a crunch,
and ate it anyway, warm from the lunch.
My eyes are on fire, I keep hitting back,
my thoughts have gone offline, I lost the track.
This late-night reply is more like a code,
I'm groggy and grumpy in this slow motion mode.
You're worried they'll topple and fall,
maybe even interrupt your dinner call.
You stand there admiring the precarious height,
but your back is screaming for a more stable white.
The driver sits slumped over his post,
Head nodding like a sleepwalker's ghost.
We inch forward through a green-lit pass,
His eyes glazed behind the steering glass.
You left your lunch behind in a damp, dark spot,
now it's been out too long to be safe to rot.
The moment you open the bag comes the smell,
your stomach turns over—your body knows well.
He says the split should be equal and fair,
but he left half his steak in the air.
When you ask about your share, he tries to shift,
and calls your portion a strange kind of gift.
You lie there sprawled on top of your bed,
your muzzle nuzzles where my arm is spread.
Warm slobber seeps into the fabric drip,
I laugh but can't help holding you in grip.
Your coffee mug sits in a coffee trace,
like a relic in this quiet space.
I almost called you just to hear your call,
but left it there, where silence hits the wall.
A smiling face glows from the billboard's face,
promising heaven in this endless place.
Its neon light warms my tired eyes tonight,
though I know its joy won't last a single might.
You think there's something in the air,
but it's just your dog giving a full glare.
You toss the nearest crumb for a treat,
he turns it into a performance feat.
You fell into bed hoping for tight sleep,
but woke with a kink where your head went too deep.
Now you're stuck at the desk, not moving from chair,
waiting for your neck to remember the air.
My dog leaned in for a snuggle on my face,
he must have thought that was his favorite place.
Now there's a wet mark blooming into a stain,
I'm trying hard not to let this ruin my brain.
The folders pile high and wobble at top,
I dread the crash that this disaster will stop.
I move to balance the mess I did try,
but panic keeps rising into the sky.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: They caught her between a frown and a face,
mid-sentence, mid-step, not her usual place.
But years from now when the light starts to grow,
she'll laugh at the timing and still want to know.
She walks barefoot just to avoid the floor,
a flip-flop still wedged in the front door.
Her socked foot taps out a steady heel,
she laughs each time the rubber makes a squeal.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: The fire pops like sparks in the heavy air,
a creak from the hallway, you pause on the stair.
You swear there's a shape in the flickering ghost,
but the room holds no answer, just you and your host.
I took a fry from your plate without being near,
you caught me and laughed into my ear.
We split the rest like we used to share,
but silence hangs between us in the air.
I keep returning to this box of old mail,
each faded message makes me feel so pale.
I trace the ink with my unsteady hand,
pretending they're from a far-off land.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You watch the sky turn from white to blue,
the horizon folds into a slow-moving view.
The breeze carries secrets it never lets hush,
while thunder rolls soft as your skin's first blush.
You sit in the kitchen, the only light,
the refrigerator hums through the night.
It feels like a lullaby, soft and call,
vibrating through cabinets, a calm down the hall.
They left the milk out—no one had a clue,
it spoiled for days, the carton turned blue.
But they stood in the kitchen, proud to let it grow,
like some weird badge of honor to put on show.
I used to skip the fine print and just read,
now every loaf feels like a kind of bread.
I check for the truth, try to know what's inside,
your face lights up when I choose it with pride.
You stare at the water, so calm and still,
but the waves don't feel right—they seem to fill
with something unseen, a slow, dark shift,
like the sky is holding a quiet rift.
They say they only had one quick mid-morning snack,
but the crumbs have launched a full QWERTY attack.
You'd think they'd fix this digital mess,
but they just send a memo without an address.
She tried to flip it but missed her try,
now the bottom's black, but she won't let it cry.
The pan still smells like sugar and burn,
yet we laugh until we both start to turn.
She climbed up the old oak tree,
hiding behind a loose branch with glee.
But she forgot it was getting late,
and missed her snack time by the gate.
I found a big clue stuck fast to my shoe,
it's a blob of old gum still soft and blue.
I try to peel it off with a quick snap,
but more comes with every slow scrap.
I feel less silly when I'm singing alone,
I mute my phone so no one hears the tone.
Steam from the water makes the mirror steam,
I belt out ballads, lost in every dream.
You set your alarm for some mythical hour,
the coffee still hasn't kicked in with power.
Your eyelids are heavy, your brain feels unwise,
you stare at the clock like it owes you a prize.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You watch every flicker go silent and flame,
It's your birthday and you're the main name.
The smoke curls up fast as you blow them all out,
The room claps like you just made a loud shout.
My show froze flat, no warning, no clue,
A loading wheel spins lazily in blue.
I beg it to load, but it won't start the show,
Just silence from the screen, and nothing below.
Your dog stands there with eyes full of bark,
convinced every minute is getting too dark.
You sigh but get out the bag for the meal,
though guilt makes the treat feel like a steal.
The meal wore off, my energy's all down,
I stare at the clock, I should get back to town.
I flip off the switch and sink into light,
but I'll dream of this peace until morning's bright.
I waited until I heard the last pop,
then turned off the alarm—never think to stop.
I poured my black coffee and tried to read,
but now there's smoke where breakfast should lead.
I see your backpack hanging by the back
of the door where you left it without a track.
You filled it with textbooks, but also a light,
a tiny flashlight from some distant night.
I used to fill this jar with something bold,
now it's a hollow, dusty vessel, cold.
It still bears the label with the brand's old name,
but it's just a relic—no flavor, no fame.
Your car radio loses all sound,
Static hits the airwaves like thunder on the ground.
You turn up the volume, still holding out hope,
Maybe it's just the signal—you'll drive and you'll cope.
She lingers in the glow of the fridge's stare,
sniffing empty shelves for expired air.
No granola bar or stale chip in her snack,
just footsteps echoing on the hunt's same track.
They brought the last-minute grocery-store dish,
pretending it was something we could all wish.
Forks clink against the chipped mismatched plate,
like this is a romantic kind of date.
You roll the window down to feel the air,
but it doesn't help with the weight of your care.
The cars zip by without even trying to pass,
and you keep your eyes fixed behind the glass.
You left the cake out in ninety-degree mess,
the heat did all the decorating in stress.
A sugar-coated drip falls from the drop,
you call it "rustic" and leave off the crop.
You put it on again like a comfort show,
no rush to move the story along slow.
This time your eyes catch what they didn't see—
a detail that makes you believe it could be.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A toddler squirms in the store's empty aisle,
her face red from the attempt to smile.
Her mother checks out a box of discount cake,
while time slips through like a long pause to break.
They land and vanish, soft as they fall,
a silent farewell the sky tries to call.
My coat remains cold, numb, and still,
though warmth says it won't, maybe it will.
The machine just won't read my crumpled-up scan,
so I revert to my old manual plan.
I miss the slow rhythm of counting out cash,
the human smile after I paid with a flash.
I found the piece that finally made the shape,
how we laughed when the edges met in escape.
We timed it just right—ten years and some time,
like climbing a mountain to find that one climb.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I hold the candle firm, it casts a fragile light,
the shadows shrink a little in the night.
There's so much farther to go, but I see more,
the flicker in my hand is worth the door.
She checks the fridge door again for the glass,
but it's been days since she poured it or pass.
Her cereal is soggy—she knows it too well,
yet the carton just shows her an empty shell.
She makes the paper breathe with every move,
her hand in perfect rhythm, steady groove.
With charcoal in her grip, she finds the shade,
and lifts a cloud to take its place in parade.
She left her laundry in the corner to spill,
not knowing she'd move out before it would still.
She sighed but said it wasn't worth the mess,
a part of the old life she couldn't redress.
I leave the kitchen light on for its soft glow,
it's just a habit I don't even really know.
It hums along when I'm the only one alone,
casting shadows where my flickering phone has grown.
You circle the important stuff in red ink,
then cross out the lies you swore you wouldn't think.
Your coffee stained the corner, smearing the date,
but somehow it still feels like everything's fate.
You're still waiting for that missing phone to call,
you've pried up floorboards and checked every wall.
A sock holds a snack, but gives no new clue,
yet you know it's out there, just waiting for you.
You think you're winning the war with the sun,
like walking barefoot is some secret fun.
Your soles will scream of that brief, sweet ache,
and you'll wish for shoes on this concrete break.
They left their receipts in a total mess,
Each pile whispers "No," but they said it was a yes.
I tried to sort them out, but I couldn't take
The madness — it's less a bill and more a cake.
I stare into space from my frozen chair,
each muscle still locked from the last half-hour there.
The neck crack is loud, but it's not enough—no click
will fix what I owe to this lousy old trick.
You think there's some app or trick to be fix,
but your phone just hums in pixelated mix.
You tap it, you wiggle it—pray for a tap
of life while it sits at the saddest 1% cap.
You doomscroll through your endless hate feed,
each post more unhinged than the last one you read.
They claim they're fighting for truth or for war,
while you laugh and swipe them right off the door.
His fingers slide through every tune,
the sidewalk echoes under the moon.
He grins when someone tosses a song,
I clap and stomp if only to sing along.
Your screen flashes slow like the edge of the doom,
you pace through the house for a better room.
The video keeps freezing, it's nothing but lag,
you blame every device in your tech-filled bag.
You stood there proud of your brand-new mess,
no way to explain it, no email or address.
The stain grew bolder, a permanent mark,
but you wore it like armor, light or dark.
She thinks she knows where the shadows will go,
but the sun won't show up till morning's slow.
Her plants beg for light, heads too proud to burn,
while she grumbles at how they won't just turn.
She says something dull but begins to joke,
her face twists with a laugh that she can't choke.
It's not even funny, but here it goes real,
like a hiccup of joy from some old lost meal.
The playlist's stuck and it won't let the song play,
It loops the chorus like some cruel delay.
You tap and swipe but it just can't figure why,
As if the music might vanish and die.
Her alarm goes off like a siren or clock,
Each blaring beep feels like a rude shock.
She tries to rise but her brain still lies,
In dreams of sleep, her ambition meets demise.
Their eyes fly open at the blaring alarm,
They dream they were sleeping on a quiet farm.
They stretch with a smile, full of false hope,
And fumble for coffee like a lifeline rope.
You've checked the couch, the bed, the bathroom floor,
retraced the walk where you dropped them and tore.
Every sock, every jacket holds no clue,
and the music fades out now, just like you.
He should've stayed off the couch and the bed,
but your dog insists on dropping his head.
You laugh when he licks you instead of the mess,
and let him keep his little puddle-shaped guess.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: You click the photo tagged to that old street,
where every neighbor's porch light was a feat.
The walls still hum with the scent of your glow,
but now it's strangers living your old show.
You push against the door, it won't feel tight,
the exit sign glows green, but still feels light.
The teacher's lecture drones on without class,
you count the minutes till you can stamp your pass.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She didn't know her face was caught mid-grin,
the way the light stretched her out quite too thin.
He looks away, a shadowed kind of sigh,
pretending not to frame it as a lie.
You can't find a seat so you grip the pole to stand,
someone's elbow bumps your coffee with their hand.
A kid jogs down the aisle to get off at the pass,
their juice box leaks right onto your phone case's glass.
The light spreads across the glassy blue glow,
silent and cold on the untouched morning snow.
A fissure appears where the ice starts to crack,
you hold your breath but the lake holds it back.
I watched him sneeze when he first saw the face,
the icing shaped just for this special place.
He sniffed, then ran with the whole thing to eat,
while I laughed, heart heavy with love and meat.
You're chasing bubbles leaving nothing but a mess,
one popped right on your face, now smudged across your dress.
The soap is gone, the fun's already done,
why did you promise me you'd never let them run?
You never admit you cry during the song,
but your voice cracks when the chorus is too strong.
Your tears drip into the cup, a quiet stream,
while the lyrics promise love can still redeem.
You hear the first soft drop hit the crack,
like a secret no one else could track.
It smells like home, like old wooden smell,
and every puddle feels like an empty shell.
Your phone starts humming through the dinner wave,
I barely know you but I somehow still crave
the sight of you holding that strange new tone,
thinking maybe I never want to be alone.
He wipes the fog away with one fast, wrong slow,
the whole thing's blurred, but he insists he can go.
I don't know why he thinks he has a clue,
he drives like he can see the road in clear view.
A single ketchup drop becomes a mess,
It stains her white shirt and her brand-new dress.
She jabs at the spoon, but it keeps to drip,
She tries to catch it, but just can't get a grip.
You tiptoe outside to view the frost's fine art,
it sparkles like your dog's excited heart.
The lawn becomes a quilt in winter's gold,
you pause just long enough to let it hold.
You watch the steam twist upward toward your face,
unsure if it's smoke or a ghost in its place.
Your hands shake as you reach for the call,
but the water boils out and hits the wall.
You blow them gently, pinky in the blue,
they pop beneath your feet before you go through.
You don't stop running even when they all fall,
I try to get your attention but you don't call.
It sits there perfect, a golden-brown glow,
my counter's new star, and I want the world to know.
I left it out just to watch it turn fruit,
like a chef's prize catch, or a treasure trove's loot.
I found your sticky note still on the chair,
the ink a little faded, but you're still there.
There's a stick figure smiling through its face,
and scribbled underneath — *Don't forget this place*.
The clock says it's late, but your thumb still moves late,
past memes and likes, through the endless gate.
Your eyes feel heavy, yet the feed denies,
how tired you are as you scroll through lies.
Your phone insists it knows exactly where to lead,
even though this road looks oddly dead.
You check your map app with a confused face,
but it still claims this is the perfect place.
You've been hunched over the keyboard all time,
your back feels like it's about to become a climb.
Every muscle protests, stiff and grumbly ache,
so you roll your shoulders for a much-needed break.
The plumber left a sticky note on the door,
It warned of rust, high bills, and more.
You tried to pretend you heard nothing but sleep,
Until the bill made you take a giant leap.
We met here once, but now they're not the same,
just shadows of the ones who used that name.
They haunt my stories, never seen as ghost,
just missing from the dinner I still host.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: It sits right there, attached to the pole with flair,
the kind of lock you'd laugh at in the air.
There's no hint of theft, not even a clue,
just style over safety, so proud in its view.
A plastic bag flaps wildly in the air,
dancing like a ghost lost in its hair.
It tangles in the hedge with bits of fluff,
catching sun as if it's full of stuff.
You run out of things to say but keep it talk,
your voice soft as you walk along the walk.
You gesture like maybe you mean to take their hand,
but it lands instead in your pocket, unplanned.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She cranks up the radio and hits replay,
the tune takes her back to a summer day.
She sways in her seat, she matches the speed,
and belts out the chorus right into the lead.
The conveyor belt spins, but the items won't scan,
she adjusts them twice with the same old plan.
A long line forms, and she's visibly alone,
while the cashier sighs in a strained, deadpan tone.
The air bites through my socks, so thin, so cold,
I was told this place would never really hold.
My boots leave prints where steam should hit the floor,
I close the door tighter, like I can seal the sore.
You stirred the soup while I tried to catch my air,
your hair fell loose where my hands wandered there.
We never spoke but the silence was a beat,
slow as cinnamon simmering into heat.
She flips the tape and starts to rewind the whole roll,
pressing play mid-memory, dancing her old soul.
The hiss and crackle fill the room so deep,
she falls asleep before they get to the "sleep."
You chose this shortcut through the rocky path,
now you wish you were home taking a bath.
Your tires keep skidding and you fear a spin,
why did you think this was a good trip to begin?

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You posted the joke again into thin air,
clearly didn't bother to check who was there.
It landed with a thud, another sad fail,
now everyone's rolling their eyes down the trail.
I squeeze the old tube like it's a precious waste,
half mint and memory, stale on my taste.
I'll savor this habit till the paste is the last,
of mornings, of mirrors, of love in the past.
They sent me an email with shocking new news,
it says I've been racking up data from use.
I never agreed to this sneaky new plan,
and now I'm just cringing at how much it ran.
She brags she got the last chip in the air,
but you still hand it to her from your pair.
You laugh when she sighs and pretends to bend,
like that little fight could ever have an end.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: You're sitting here with your tired face and your sit,
a half-finished thought that won't quite fit.
The cold coffee chills, a quiet little shame,
untouched now, like someone else's old name.
They leaned in close and spoke it all out,
no raised voice, just raw truths they shout.
They found a way to hold the whole day,
heavy as it was, they made it okay.
You watch her come each morning through the gate,
her collar jingles softly, never late.
She tilts her head when you say her name, your face
is where she wants to be, her favorite place.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: She turns the key in the rusted old lock,
dust rises like ghosts from the box's stock.
Her fingers shake as she reaches her hand,
for a moment, time stops where her courage stand.
You sink into sleep where the cushions are deep,
A dream hums along while the hours you keep.
The sun climbs the wall, your body begins to rise,
You leave it behind, more awake, more wise.
She mutters about her weak and sour blend,
"This isn't worth the time it took to mend."
She grounds beans with a frown and bitter taste,
then throws out the old pot—complete waste.
She stood there once, all wide-eyed and before,
now even the sky calls it a chore.
The rain runs quick where the heat had been,
but she's not the one who'll ever let it in.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: A pop song plays on in his private tune,
he hums along with the radio's weak moon.
It loops in his head from dusk 'til through,
like static stuck there where memories used to glue.
She gives me the look — *totally* no clue,
her coffee's gone cold while she stares at the brew.
"I'll clean them this week," she says with a call,
then texts me a photo of the same dusty wall.
You see the name on your lips but not on the face,
you swear they were here, but forget where the place.
You promise yourself you'll never again lose
the way memory slips off like mismatched shoes.
Her jelly-smeared hands leave a trail of mess,
She's smudged her white dress and she doesn't stress.
The sandwich slips once, she loses her grip,
It lands jelly-side up in her lunchbox slip.
It hangs in midair, completely still,
defying wind, gravity, its will.
One twitch and it's gone—just a flash, a dart,
a fleeting masterpiece, never to be part.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You run your finger along every trace,
towns faded softly from their old place.
The ink still maps out each winding mile,
you dream of roads that might have been while.
They wake up to the steady sound,
a quiet rhythm in their ground.
The fridge hums soft in the kitchen's light,
a comfort that outlasts the night.
You call it a growl when it's really just time,
a crack that won't hide, and it starts to climb.
You say "it adds flavor," but deep down you know
the voice you once loved now barely will go.
I wobble in slow motion toward the back,
the tires scream like they want another track.
My knees begin to throb, a certain ache,
I hit the ground. I need to fix my brake.
The app can't match the smile to the face,
it lingers, confused, in some strange place.
But you know who they are without a clue—
your eyes remember what systems can't make true.
It slips through the branches like time turning gold,
I try to catch moments the light tries to hold.
It flickers across my tired, familiar face,
but the glow won't stay here or in any one place.
The trailer ends with a creaking door,
leaving questions we can't ignore.
A stranger's face appears in the frame,
and vanishes before I can name.

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: You lose your right sock—where's the other soul?
You dig through the heap, your hands frantically scroll.
They promised a match but returned only a pile,
now you're limping through life, one shoe per mile.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: You pat the cushions, then you find some cash,
crumpled and warm from its hiding place stash.
Your eyes light up as your smile turns to grin,
you plan your weekend and where it will begin.
She walks a mile an hour below my pace,
I scan the sidewalk for her missing trace.
She disappears around some corner ahead,
I check my phone—no signal, just trees and dread.
She clings to the fragile thread of hope,
her patience fraying like an old rope.
Days blur together, time won't go through,
and all she feels now is the sky's quiet blue.
You swore you'd check in just five minutes from then,
but your phone buzzed once more, dismissed again.
You tap the window, watch the ants on the glass,
while summer slips off into the next grass.
She tightens the band and tries to hold,
her muscles protest but she won't fold.
Her breath comes out in shaky little puff,
yet confidence grows where doubt once was stuff.
He fumbles through pockets at the turnstile gate,
the train's already gone and he's minutes late.
His ticket's still tucked in his jacket's left fold,
but now every station feels dead and so cold.
She digs through her bag but leaves no trace,
guilt flickers across her tired face.
A crumb at the bottom still clings to the raid,
she zips up and hopes the smell will fade.
The foil peels off like yesterday's great fail,
leaving silver tears in a zigzag trail.
There's no clear reason, no logic or clue—
just another mess the grocery store sold you.
You leave your shoes by the door just to show,
they're polished clean, still wearing their glow.
It's a quiet way to say you take care,
and now there's nowhere else you'd rather be there.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You sat down beside me, way too near,
your voice a soft whisper in my ear.
I tried to pretend I didn't miss
the moment when silence almost was a kiss.
You used to move like music had a flow,
now you freeze when the DJ starts to show.
You count each step, the rhythm feels off-beat,
your face burns with the flash of stage heat.
You spend hours trying out every name,
It's not funny anymore—it's just a game.
You loop through the options stuck in your mind,
But nothing feels right, so you let it unwind.
You're trapped in the seat by the window, aisle,
ten more hours till your next food mile.
The kids are loud and the coffee's got gas,
you vow you'll never travel this pass.
I love to scan the back of every can,
searching for secrets I want to plan.
I think I should know what's inside this dough—
the label says "flavor," but won't just show.
You kept trying to match my forced little grin,
the silence was loud in this noisy little din.
We sat in the front row, wedged in the aisle,
asked about the plot just to fake a smile.
You want your thoughts to feel clean and clear,
you hum an old song to warm up your ear.
You turn on the fan, switch on the light,
and hope today will work out alright.
I turn the fan up but the room stays on heat,
I toss again, this motion feels like a repeat.
There's no reason to lie—I don't have a clue,
the pillow says everything about me and you.
I slow down just enough to try to bend,
my pulse is loud like thoughts that won't send.
One false move now will guarantee a trip,
but the laces slip and never give a grip.
The zipper won't budge as I try to climb,
you reach back gently and help me in time.
We laugh like old friends finding the thread,
"Let's take it slow, love," is all that you said.
Her screen glows once, a last weak call,
it's too late now to try them all.
The light begins to slowly fade,
the phone just dies, the hope is laid.
I tried to hold on but lost all my grip,
slipped on the railing and took a bad trip.
I wipe off the syrup, still feel the trace,
of summer on metal, and sugar on face.
I watch him spin in his nightly loop,
no army of mice follows this troop.
His whiskers twitch through the dust in his fur,
while I lie awake and can't seem to stir.
She walks alone where the restless sea turns calm,
Her breath like salt air, a needed balm.
The sky is bleeding into gold and light,
The horizon stretches out beyond her sight.
You follow the ants as if it's your new path,
trying to count them, basic ant math.
They don't ask for your help to crawl,
yet you map their entire tiny sprawl.
You left the theater with eyes still dry,
the kind of sad that matches stormy sky.
You wanted someone to hug you and hold,
but no one needed the plot to be told.
I was trying to make something look like art,
but the colors ran wild like a rainbow chart.
My floor now has blue from the brush's mess,
and a streak of red ruins my white new dress.
